items.text: Example: $V$ a discrete valuation ring ($\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, $k[t]_{(p)}$, $k[[t]]$): two primes, $0\subset\mathfrak m$; $\operatorname{Spec}V$ = generic point and special point, not discrete, not artinian ($\mathfrak m\supset\mathfrak m^2\supset\cdots$).
Sources of artinian schemes
\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{\,n+1}\bigr)\ \ \text{infinitesimal neighborhood of order }n\text{ of }x
I_k=\coprod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Spec}k\quad(I\text{ finite})
G\ \text{of finite type over }k:\qquad G/G^0\ \text{artinian},\qquad 1\to G^0\to G\to G/G^0\to 1
Reduced and integral schemes
Reduced: $\mathcal O_X$ has no nilpotent section $\neq0$ over any open set; equivalently the local rings $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ are reduced.
X=\operatorname{Spec}A\ \text{reduced}\iff A\ \text{reduced};\qquad A\subset\prod_{\mathfrak p}A_{\mathfrak p}
Integral: reduced and irreducible (not a local property).
$X=\bigcup X_i$, $X_i\neq\varnothing$: $X$ integral $\iff$ the $X_i$ are integral and meet pairwise.
X=\operatorname{Spec}A\ \text{integral}\iff A\ \text{integral domain}\qquad(\operatorname{Spec}A\ \text{irreducible}\iff A/\mathrm{nil}(A)\ \text{integral})
Normal schemes
$A$ integrally closed: every $x\in K=\operatorname{Frac}A$ integral over $A$ lies in $A$.
$X$ normal: all local rings $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ are integrally closed domains. $X$ locally noetherian $\Rightarrow$ disjoint union of integral schemes.
$X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ integral: normal $\iff$ $A$ integrally closed in its field of fractions.
Geometric meaning (Zariski's main theorem)
$X$ noetherian integral, generic point $\eta$; $K=\kappa(\eta)$ the field of rational functions.
$f\colon X'\to X$ of finite type, $X'$ integral, is birational if $\eta'\mapsto\eta$ and $K\to K'$ is an isomorphism; equivalently
\exists\,U\subset X\ \text{open non-empty}:\quad f^{-1}(U)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }U
$X$ normal $\iff$ every birational $f\colon X'\to X$ of finite type with finite fibres is locally an open immersion (an open immersion if moreover separated).
Counterexamples to drop « finite fibres »: blow-up of a point of the plane (fibre $\mathbf P^1$ = projectivised tangent space).
Node: normalization separates the two branches, two points over the double point, $X$ not normal.
Cusp: normalization is a bijection, not an isomorphism; the local ring is not a discrete valuation ring.
Converse: the normalization $X'\to X$ is birational with finite fibres; if it is an isomorphism, $X$ is normal.
Regular schemes
$X$ regular: all local rings are regular local rings.
Over an algebraically closed field $k$, $X$ of finite type: $x$ is regular iff
\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\simeq k[[t_1,\dots,t_n]]\quad\text{as a }k\text{-algebra}
Regular local ring $A$: noetherian, and there exist $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\mathfrak m$ forming a regular sequence,
x_1\ \text{injective on }A,\ \ x_2\ \text{injective on }A/x_1A,\ \dots,\ x_n\ \text{injective on }A/(x_1A+\dots+x_{n-1}A),\qquad A/\textstyle\sum_i x_iA=k
The $x_i$ generate $\mathfrak m$: local coordinates. (An $M$-regular sequence: $x_1$ injective on $M$, $x_2$ on $M/x_1M$, etc.; the Koszul complex is acyclic.)
Examples of regular rings
A field is regular; $A$ regular $\Rightarrow$ $A[t]$ regular; hence $k[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ and $\mathbf G_m$, $\mathrm{GL}_n$ are regular schemes.
Localization: if $A$ is a regular local ring, so is $A_{\mathfrak p}$ (Serre: regular $\iff$ finite global dimension).
Any principal ideal domain or Dedekind ring is regular: $\mathbf Z$, rings of integers of number fields, and polynomial rings over them.
A\ \text{noetherian local}:\quad A\ \text{regular}\iff\widehat A\ \text{regular}
O\ \text{complete local},\ k\subset O\to\kappa\ \text{iso}:\quad O\ \text{regular}\iff O\simeq k[[t_1,\dots,t_n]]
$A$ regular noetherian $\Rightarrow$ $A[[t]]$ regular.
$A\to A[t]$, $P\mapsto q$: $A[t]_P$ is a localization of $A_q[t]$, hence regular when $A$ is.
